thread:
maria: FYI customer org-redwood-42 says their GCP Marketplace invoice line items don't line up with our usage dashboard. They see a $3,200 charge labeled 'Redwood Inference (Marketplace)' but our dashboard shows ~$2,600 for the same period.

sam: Got it. Can you paste the invoice number + marketplace order id? Also need the date range and a screenshot of our usage UI.

maria: Invoice: INV-2026-03-98, marketplace order id: 0123456789ABCDEF. Date range: 2026-02-01 to 2026-02-28. Screenshot uploaded -> https://internal.s3/redwood/support/2026-03/recon-screens-42.png

alisa: Quick hypotheses: marketplace often bills differently — could be markup/fees, taxes, or they meter different dimensions (e.g., VM-hours or API calls vs token usage). Also watch timezone/aggregation windows.

kevin: Finance note: AWS/GCP sometimes show a single umbrella line item for the Marketplace listing which includes pass-through charges + our usage + platform fees. Confirm whether the invoice includes a 'Marketplace surcharge' line. If so, amount could explain delta.

maria: Customer says the line item is just one amount, no breakdown on their end. They attached their GCP invoice PDF (gcp-invoice-0123.pdf).

sam: Ok we need to compare raw meter records. Ask customer to provide the marketplace billing export (CSV or BigQuery export) or grant us read access to the billing bucket. For AWS they'd share the S3 marketplace report. For GCP, BigQuery export or the CSV from Billing > Documents.

maria: I asked and they can share the GCP billing export. They've granted a one-time view link: gs://customer-billing-exports/org-42/2026-02-billing.csv

alisa: Can you pull a sample and compare to our internal usage export? Key things to check: meter dimension (are they counting token-units or API request units?), time granularity (hourly vs per-request), rounding/ceilings, and currency/exchange differences.

kevin: Also check commit/discounts. If the customer had a committed-use discount or reserved capacity in marketplace, charges might apply differently than our raw per-token price.

maria: I ran a quick diff. Their CSV shows a SKU with description 'Marketplace line item: redwood-inference.standard' with quantity 1000 and unit price $3.2 -> $3,200. Our export shows total tokens 8.3M and effective rate ~$0.00031/token -> ~$2,573. So quantity units don't map to tokens.

sam: That screams 'metering dimension mismatch'. Marketplace might be aggregating by 'billing unit' that equals 1 = 1k requests or 1 = hourly seat. We need the raw meter name/key from the CSV. Paste first few rows (sanitize any PII).

maria: CSV snippet: ```
invoice_id,sku,usage_start,usage_end,quantity,unit_price,currency
INV-2026-03-98,redwood-inference.standard,2026-02-01T00:00:00Z,2026-02-28T23:59:59Z,1000,3.2,USD
```

alisa: Yep. That 'quantity=1000' isn't tokens. Could be 1000 x 'marketplace-unit' where 1 unit = 1000 tokens or similar. We should map the SKU to our metering connector. I will check our marketplace metering config for the GCP listing (sku mapping file).

sam: While Alisa checks, Maria ask customer for their marketplace usage report where SKU has more detailed meter dimension (sometimes additional columns like 'usage_unit' or 'usage_amount'). Also ask if they purchased any monthly subscription/seat in Marketplace.

maria: Asked. They replied: "No seats. It's metered usage only." They attached a fuller export with column 'usage_unit' = 'billing_unit' and 'usage_amount' = 1000.

kevin: If it's purely metered, next steps: 1) map marketplace SKU -> our internal meter. 2) run a reconciliation (per-hour) aligning timezones. 3) if marketplace quantity multiplier exists (e.g., 1 billing_unit = 1k tokens), compute adjusted cost and find discrepancy. If still mismatch, escalate to GCP marketplace support.

alisa: Confirmed: in our listing we declared the meter as 'billing_unit = 1' where 1 = 1k token-block. But the marketplace reporting shows quantity already normalized differently due to an old mapping. Looks like during a past update the SKU metadata was set to 1=1k tokens while current metering sends raw tokens. That would double-count in the marketplace report.

sam: Ouch. That explains ~20% delta? Calculate: if marketplace billed 1000 units at $3.2/unit = $3,200 but those units actually represented 1k-token blocks while we billed per-token, we need to recompute. Please attach our per-hour export for 2026-02.

maria: Uploaded our export -> https://internal.s3/redwood/support/2026-03/internal-usage-42.csv

alisa: I ran a quick script and when I normalize units to the marketplace's declared 1k-token block the charges align within $10 after excluding taxes. So root cause = incorrect SKU declaration in the marketplace listing metadata.

kevin: Finance: we'll prepare a credit for the customer for the overcharged amount. Also need to inform Partnerships to update the SKU metadata and trigger a fix for future months.

tanya: Support manager: please open an internal ticket and route to #finance, #partnerships, #eng-ml (metering) and #legal if customer contract wording affected. Tag ticket as marketplace-billing-recon-2026-543.

maria: Done. Internal ticket: 2026-543. I've attached the diff, recalculation, and recommended credit amount $620. Also asked Partnerships to patch the SKU mapping and confirm when fixed.

billing-bot: label added: marketplace-recon, owner: partnerships, priority: P2

sam: Next steps for eng: push SKU metadata fix, add integration test that sanity-checks marketplace quantity vs token counts, and add alert when market-reported charge deviates >10% from our expected revenue.

alisa: I'll create a small unit test and a dashboard query. ETA EOD tomorrow.

kevin: Finance will draft credit memo and send to customer after Partnerships confirms fix. Good catch, team.

maria: Closing loop with customer now — told them we found a mapping issue, will credit, and will follow up with timeline. They appreciate the quick turnaround. :thumbsup:
